newsitem.title: USA: Musicland in pact with many large suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Musicland in pact with many large suppliers.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp said Thursday that a substantial majority of its largest suppliers have agreed to temporarily defer existing trade payables and provide continued product supply.
The agreement is subject to reduced dating terms on the new purchases. No further details were immediately available.
These understandings are voluntary on the part of the suppliers and will continue at their discretion, Musicland added.

Musicland said the agreement with suppliers gives it more time to pursue strategic alternatives to improve its financial position. As previously announced, the company hired Smith Barney to begin this process last September.

Musicland said it is pursuing a possible significant equity investment that would involve a substantial issuance of new shares and a restructuring of the company's balance sheet. However, there is no assurance that an equity investment will be made.

As announced in December, Musicland is closing poorly performing stores and will take a restructure reserve in the fourth quarter to support that program. From December through February, the company will have closed 75 stores, including 15 Media Play stores. Four more Media Play stores are scheduled to close in the first quarter of 1997.

Musicland is a specialty retailer of pre-recorded home-entertainment products in the United States. As of December 31, it operated 1,466 retail stores in 49 states, the United Kingdom, Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands under the names Media Play, On Cue, Suncoast Motion Picture Company and Sam Goody/Musicland.
